newsitem.title: USA: Georgia governor says job growth 'phenomenal'.
newsitem.headline: Georgia governor says job growth 'phenomenal'.

text.p: Georgia Gov. Zell Miller called Tuesday for strengthening marketing efforts by the Department of Industry, Trade and Tourism to improve job growth that was already "phenomenal."
Georgia saw $6.3 billion of new industrial investment announced last year, an amount expected to create more than 33,000 new jobs, the governor said in his state of the state address to legislators.

"Probably the best news for our families today is that 3.6 million Georgians have jobs, more than at any time in our history," Miller said. "We've seen phenomenal job growth -- an average of over 2,000 new jobs a week since 1990."
The govenor said the Department of Industry, Trade and Tourism had played a significant role in the expansion.
"But like all of us, they can always do better. So we are going to reorganize the Department to continue improving coordination among our economic development initiatives," Miller said.

Specifically, Miller proposed strengthening department marketing efforts as part of Operation Legacy, a public-private partnership that used the Olympics to bring chief executive officers from more than 400 companies to Georgia.

"I also propose that we bring the Governor's Development Council under the Industry and Trade umbrella in a new Strategic Planning and Research Division," Miller said. "And we will continue to encourage regional planning initiatives, with a $2.5 million grant program that supports multi-county, regional collaboration for economic development."

The governor quoted a recent Dun & Bradstreet report that called Georgia "the biggest winner in the battle to retain companies and jobs." Dun & Bradstreet attributed much of that success to the state's moderate tax rate.
Miller took part of the credit for that, noting that his administration has cut state income taxes and is phasing out the sales taxes on groceries.
